claims.text: The as-deposited melt-spun FeMnNiGeSi-type ribbons are in an ordered, single-phase hexagonal state.
Rapid solidification produces internal-stress and defect distributions in the ribbons.
Thermo-mechanical cycling near the magnetostructural transition induces a uniform internal-stress and defect landscape.
Cyclic mechanical loading redistributes preexisting internal stresses created during melt spinning.
Cyclic mechanical loading modifies preexisting defect structures created during melt spinning.
The treatment produces aligned dislocation networks and residual-strain fields.
The modified defects and residual-strain fields serve as nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
Redistributing internal stresses and defects lowers the nucleation barrier for the transformed phase.
A lower nucleation barrier promotes more cooperative domain switching.
The modified nucleation behavior enables a more gradual and broadened magnetostructural transition.
Broadening the transition reduces the hysteresis associated with the sharp first-order transition.
The as-deposited ribbons exhibit a sharp, first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited ribbons exhibit a large but hysteretic magnetic entropy change.
Relative to untreated ribbons, treated samples will show a gentler temperature dependence of magnetic entropy change across the transition.
Relative to untreated ribbons, treated samples will show significantly reduced thermal hysteresis.
Relative to untreated ribbons, treated samples will show significantly reduced magnetic hysteresis during low-field cycling.
Performing cyclic compression in an inert atmosphere will maintain phase purity and avoid oxidation.
The specified treatment ensures that internal-stress distribution is the only altered variable.
The predictions apply to melt-spun, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys with similar thermal and mechanical histories.
Changes in composition, processing route, or strain magnitude may change the effectiveness of the proposed stress-redistribution mechanism.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that the treatment ensures internal-stress distribution is the only altered variable, whereas the mediator and mechanism explicitly predict modification of defect structures, including dislocation networks.
The conditions assert isolation of internal stress as the only changed variable, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that other microstructural changes could contribute.
